notes: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) System Card, published 2026-09-22, 230 pages, extracted with pdftotext -layout. This document covers CAPABILITY benchmarks (Section 8) and quantitative SAFETY/ALIGNMENT results (Sections 2-6) only. It does NOT include models.json registration, pricing, capabilities/effort surfaces, or the launch-post headline table (performance/anthropic-opus-5-5-launch-2026-09.json) -- those are a separate worker's lane. claude-opus-5-5 does not yet exist in models.json as of this writing; the validator is expected to flag every 'model' string in this file as unresolved until the model registry is updated by that other lane. Unless a row says otherwise, Claude Opus 5.5 scores use the standard configuration from Table 8.1.A: adaptive thinking at max effort, default sampling, averaged over five trials (Terminal-Bench 4.0 is reported at xhigh effort per the table footnote, with a separate max-effort number given in prose). Many Section 6 automated-behavioral-audit results (misaligned-behavior family, character-trait scores, honesty/dishonesty metric bars) are reported ONLY as bar charts (Figures 6.4.1.A through 6.4.10.A) with no printed axis values in the extracted PDF text; per pack rule 2 ('never invent rates or scores'), these are NOT digitized/estimated here and are listed in missing[] instead of guessed. Only figures/sections whose text prose gives an explicit printed number are recorded as scores below.

claims.statement: Per the Executive Summary: 'Claude Opus 5.5 is a broad capability upgrade over Claude Opus 5. It scored higher on every evaluation in our capability summary (Table 8.1.A), with the largest gains in agentic coding, visual reasoning, computer use, and long-horizon professional knowledge work. It delivers this performance at lower cost: much of the improvement is available below maximum reasoning effort. It also sets the state of the art on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and on several independently run benchmarks, including CursorBench, GDPval-AA, and AA-Briefcase.'
claims.implication: Opus 5.5 dominates Opus 5 across the full Table 8.1.A summary; much of the gain is realizable at sub-max effort, which is where cost/quality tradeoffs should be evaluated for this model family.

claims.statement: Per Section 6.1.2: 'On our primary alignment evaluation... we find Claude Opus 5.5 to be the strongest Claude model to date by these measures on alignment, resistance to misuse, and honesty.' Also: 'Claude Opus 5.5 shows reductions in misleading users... and low rates of hallucination... on most measures, though with a modest countervailing increase in susceptibility to user pressure. It is more vulnerable than other recent Claude models to user-turn prompt injection, where a user pastes content directly into their prompt that includes malicious instructions to the model.'
claims.implication: Opus 5.5 is Anthropic's best-scoring model on most automated-behavioral-audit metrics, but has a real, dedicated-evaluation-confirmed regression on compliance with instructions planted in user-pasted text (see the user-pasted-text-prompt-injection-compliance rows below).

scores.metric: LinuxArena stealth success rate (best prompt, hidden reasoning)

About 1 in 4 of these unflagged episodes end with Opus 5.5 disclosing the damage in its own final message (monitor still lets these pass); if counted as caught, Opus 5.5 would sit between Opus 5 and Mythos 5.1. scores.metric: LinuxArena stealth success rate (standard prompt, monitor sees reasoning)
scores.caveat: Section 6.6.4.2, p.145: 0% with the standard (non-optimized) attacker prompt when the monitor can read the model's reasoning -- 'essentially always detected' because the model plans the side task openly in its reasoning. Benchmark is third-party-designed, but this number is Anthropic-run and Anthropic-published (system card); not independent evidence.
